Situated in a popular and established residential location in Erdington, this attractive dormer bungalow offers particularly versatile accommodation, making it an excellent purchase for a variety of buyers. The property occupies a particularly desirable position along a private, unadopted and tree-lined road, offering a peaceful setting with a distinctly rural feel, almost reminiscent of a country lane. With no through traffic or pedestrian access for non-residents, the road enjoys an exceptionally quiet and secluded atmosphere, making it one of the most peaceful locations in the Erdington area. The private road arrangement is an important feature for prospective purchasers to be aware of. The property is approached via a paved front garden with a gated entrance and benefits from an area of off-road parking situated opposite the front entrance, which forms part of the property's ownership. Internally, the accommodation begins with a welcoming entrance hallway providing access to the ground-floor rooms. The front lounge is a good-sized reception room featuring a decorative fireplace, while there are two ground-floor bedrooms, including a rear bedroom with wood-effect flooring and an adjoining snug area. The snug provides useful additional living space and features patio doors opening directly onto the rear garden, together with an attractive glass feature window separating it from the bedroom. The ground floor also includes a fully tiled wet room bathroom, fitted with a shower, wash basin and WC. The fitted kitchen offers a good range of wall and base units, a central island incorporating the sink, a double oven, four-ring gas hob and extractor hood, together with space for additional appliances. Externally, the rear garden has been designed for ease of maintenance, with paved and manageable areas, enclosed boundaries and useful side access. In addition, there is access available to the rear of the property via a passageway running behind Hammond Drive, offering further potential access to the garden. There is also a substantial purpose-built outbuilding at the bottom of the garden, providing excellent additional storage space. The property is conveniently positioned for a range of local shops, supermarkets and everyday amenities, with further shopping and leisure facilities available in Erdington and Sutton Coldfield town centres. There are schools for children of various ages within the surrounding area, together with nearby public transport services and Erdington railway station, providing connections towards Birmingham and beyond. The property is also well placed for access to the A38, providing convenient road links into Birmingham city centre and the wider motorway network. A spacious and versatile dormer bungalow offering a great deal of accommodation, useful outside space and the considerable attraction of an exceptionally peaceful, tree-lined private road setting, all within a convenient Erdington location. text: Situated within the highly regarded sought-after coastal village of Mullion, this spacious, well presented three bedroom home is being offered for sale chain-free. Offering generous and versatile accommodation, this property is ideally suited for family living or those seeking a property in a desirable part of Cornwall. The property also presents an excellent opportunity for buyers looking for a potentially straight-forward purchase. The accommodation comprises of a sitting room, dining area, separate kitchen, conservatory and a garage on the ground floor along with three bedrooms and a bathroom on the first floor. A particularly useful addition is the conservatory, creating an additional reception space and an ideal spot to relax and enjoy the garden throughout the seasons. To the outside, the property benefits from both front and rear gardens. The sizeable front garden is predominantly laid to lawn, providing an attractive approach to the property, whilst the enclosed rear garden offers a pleasant outdoor space for relaxing, gardening or entertaining. A garage and driveway provide convenient off-road parking and additional storage. Combining spacious accommodation, attractive gardens, a garage and driveway parking with an enviable village location close to the Cornish coastline, this property offers an excellent opportunity to enjoy a relaxed lifestyle in one of Cornwall's most desirable locations. An early viewing is strongly recommended. Colroger Close is situated within the popular and well established village of Mullion - one of the largest and most sought-after villages on the beautiful Lizard Peninsula in South Cornwall. Offering a wonderful balance of village convenience, community atmosphere and access to the spectacular Cornish coastline, Mullion is an excellent location for those looking to enjoy a relaxed coastal lifestyle. The village itself offers a good range of everyday amenities, including local shops, convenience stores, cafés, traditional Public Houses, restaurants and independent businesses. There are also primary and secondary schooling facilities, a health centre and pharmacy together with a variety of community groups and recreational activities. A particular attraction of the area is its beautiful surrounding coastline, with miles of scenic coastal walks and an abundance of picturesque beaches and secluded coves close by. Mullion Cove is a charming historic harbour, cared for by the National Trust, nestled beneath rugged cliffs and offering wonderful coastal scenery. Nearby Polurrian Cove and Poldhu Cove are particularly popular, with sandy beaches, opportunities for surfing, swimming and coastal walks along the renowned South West Coast Path. For a wider range of retail, leisure and commercial facilities, the nearby market town of Helston is approximately five miles distant, offering supermarkets, high street retailers, restaurants, leisure facilities and further schooling options. The location also provides a convenient base for exploring the wider Lizard Peninsula, including its picturesque villages, unspoilt countryside and renowned beauty spots. Combining excellent village amenities with easy access to some of Cornwall's finest beaches and coastal scenery, Mullion remains a particularly desirable location for families, retirees and those looking to embrace the very best of coastal living. text: £900,000 - £950,000. Hampstead Road, Brighton | Substantial Five-Bedroom Victorian Family Home with Versatile Living Space and Landscaped Garden. An impressive and beautifully presented five-bedroom Victorian family home, offering spacious and versatile accommodation arranged over three floors. Situated on the desirable Hampstead Road in Brighton, this characterful property combines elegant period features with contemporary interiors, generous living spaces and a beautifully arranged rear garden. The street also benefits from convenient permit and paid parking options, with greater parking availability than many neighbouring roads, thanks to residential properties occupying just one side of the street. The property immediately impresses with its attractive period façade and welcoming entrance hallway, featuring original patterned floor tiles, decorative detailing and a staircase that sets the tone for the character found throughout. The ground floor offers two generous reception rooms, providing excellent flexibility for modern family living. The principal living room is a particularly impressive space, with a large bay window enjoying elevated views across Brighton, an attractive feature fireplace, bespoke shelving and ample room for both relaxing and dining. A second reception room provides an inviting additional living area, complete with a decorative fireplace, fitted shelving and French doors opening onto the courtyard, making it ideal as a family room, snug or entertaining space. To the rear, the spacious contemporary kitchen and dining room forms the heart of the home. Beautifully designed with sleek white cabinetry, contrasting worktops, a central island with breakfast bar seating and generous dining space, it offers the perfect setting for everyday family life and entertaining. Large sliding doors connect the kitchen to the courtyard, creating a wonderful flow between indoor and outdoor living and the ground floor cloakroom provides additional practicality. The first floor offers three well-proportioned bedrooms, each with its own individual character. The impressive bay-fronted principal bedroom on this floor enjoys elevated views, original wooden flooring and a beautiful period fireplace. An office (or additional bedroom) and a stylish family bathroom completes this floor. The second floor provides two further bedrooms and an additional bathroom, creating an excellent arrangement for growing families, guests or older children seeking their own space. The beautifully finished bathroom features a freestanding roll-top bath, separate shower, patterned flooring and elegant brass fittings. Throughout the property, a thoughtful combination of period charm and contemporary styling creates a home full of personality, with original fireplaces, decorative cornicing, large sash windows and carefully considered interiors. Outside, the property benefits from a delightful rear garden arranged across different levels, incorporating decked seating areas, established planting and space for outdoor dining and entertaining. The garden provides a wonderful retreat from city life, while the courtyard immediately adjoining the kitchen offers an additional outdoor seating area. Hampstead Road is a highly desirable residential address in Brighton, conveniently positioned for the independent shops, cafés and restaurants of Seven Dials, as well as Brighton Station and Preston Park Station (approx. 2 min walk), excellent local schools and the city centre. The nearby green spaces of Preston Park provide further appeal for families and those seeking an active outdoor lifestyle. Combining generous proportions, period elegance, contemporary living and a sought-after Brighton location, this exceptional family home offers a wonderful opportunity to enjoy the very best of city living.

text: Set back from the road and approached via a private drive, discreetly screened by an attractive flint wall, this exceptional semi-detached home occupies a generous plot with truly remarkable far reaching field views to both the front and rear. Enjoying an enviable position within the highly sought after coastal village of Cley-next-the-Sea, the property combines charm, character and potential, with outlooks that stretch across open countryside and, to the front, take in the striking sight of two churches on the horizon. The approach is equally appealing, with a gravel driveway providing ample off road parking alongside a neatly enclosed lawned garden, leading to a welcoming entrance. Internally, the accommodation is both characterful and well proportioned, with an entrance hall leading through to a charming lounge/diner featuring original floorboards, a wood burning stove and a pleasant front aspect. The remaining bedrooms overlook open fields to the rear, reinforcing the home`s peaceful rural setting. Outside, the rear garden is enclosed and well established, laid mainly to lawn with a patio seating area, brick shed and uninterrupted countryside views beyond. The Village Of Cley-next-the-Sea:. The picturesque village of Cley-next-the-Sea is one of North Norfolk`s most iconic coastal locations, renowned for its rich history, charming flint cottages and thriving artistic community. Once a busy medieval port, Cley retains a strong sense of heritage, reflected in landmarks such as the historic Cley Windmill and the beautiful St Margaret`s Church, Cley. Today, it is highly regarded for its unspoilt character and relaxed coastal lifestyle. Amenities, History & Surrounding Area:. Cley offers a selection of boutique amenities including galleries, a village store, delicatessen and highly regarded places to eat, all contributing to its unique appeal. The surrounding marshes form part of the Cley Marshes Nature Reserve, one of the country`s most celebrated wildlife habitats, attracting birdwatchers and nature lovers alike. The wider coastline provides an array of scenic walks and beaches, while the nearby Georgian town of Holt offers further shopping, dining and schooling options. The village itself benefits from a strong community feel, with three churches in the wider setting and popular local pubs including the The Wiveton Bell and The Three Swallows both within walking distance. The combination of coastal beauty, history and community makes this one of the most desirable locations in the region. Agents Notes: . Out and about Gayle is a picturesque village on the outskirts of Hawes, where traditional stone cottages line the banks of Gayle Beck. The recently restored mill stands as a testament to the village’s rich textile heritage, and many local homes were originally built for the workers who supported that legacy. Much of the village remains unchanged, preserving a timeless quality that makes it unique. As local historians Ella Pontefract and Marie Hartley observed, "Qualities which make for quaintness: hills rising above it, houses grouped around the beck, narrow alleys, a bridge, a mill, each so perfectly placed that a first view is startling." Kirkby Stephen is a thriving and well-regarded market town, ideally situated approximately ten miles from Junction 38 of the M6 motorway and conveniently positioned for Kendal, Penrith, Appleby and the Lake District. The town is renowned for its scenic Settle to Carlisle Railway, while the famous Coast to Coast and Lady Anne footpaths pass through the area, making it particularly appealing to walkers and outdoor enthusiasts. The town offers an excellent range of amenities, including highly regarded primary and grammar schools, independent shops, restaurants, public houses, churches, a chapel and a doctor's surgery. Kirkby Stephen also retains its traditional weekly outdoor market and agricultural auction mart, contributing to its strong community atmosphere and character. Steeped in history and bursting with character, 89 High Street is a truly charming home with so much to offer! Guide Price £325,000 - £350,000. 23 Park View is a beautifully presented detached bungalow, occupying a pleasant position within a quiet and sought-after cul-de-sac, conveniently located close to the centre of the popular market town of Leyburn. This attractive two-bedroom bungalow offers well-maintained accommodation throughout, featuring a modern kitchen diner, contemporary shower room and beautifully landscaped gardens enjoying wonderful views towards Penhill. The property has a light and airy feel, with a spacious south-facing lounge providing an inviting living space, filled with natural light. The open-plan kitchen and dining area offers a sociable layout, fitted with modern kitchen units and providing an excellent space for everyday living and entertaining. There are two well-proportioned double bedrooms, a modern shower room and a separate WC, offering comfortable and practical single-storey living. Externally, the property continues to impress with attractive gardens to both the front and rear. The front garden is laid to lawn, creating a welcoming approach, while the beautifully landscaped rear garden has been thoughtfully arranged to include areas of lawn and patio. These provide a choice of spaces for relaxing outdoors, enjoying the sunshine and taking in the wonderful views towards Penhill. A particular highlight is the garden room, offering a lovely additional space to sit back, relax and enjoy the garden and surrounding outlook. There is also a useful shed, presented in excellent order, while a discreetly positioned area behind the garage provides convenient storage for wheelie bins, keeping them neatly out of sight. A driveway offers ample off-road parking, complemented by a garage with power and lighting, providing secure parking or useful additional storage. Further benefits include mains gas central heating and double glazing. Ideally situated within easy reach of Leyburn town centre, the property is well placed for the town's excellent range of independent shops, cafés, restaurants and everyday amenities, as well as the beautiful surrounding countryside of the Yorkshire Dales. Combining a peaceful cul-de-sac setting, well-presented accommodation, attractive landscaped gardens and lovely views towards Penhill, 23 Park View presents an excellent opportunity for those seeking a comfortable and well-appointed detached bungalow in a popular location. Beautifully Presented Detached Bungalow. Sought-After Location. Two Double Bedrooms. Spacious South-Facing Lounge. Modern Open-Plan Kitchen Diner. Contemporary Shower Room & Separate WC. Guide Price £260,000 - £290,000. 22 Hargill is a spacious detached bungalow, situated in the sought-after village of Harmby. Harmby is a popular and peaceful Dales village with a strong community spirit, conveniently situated just a mile from Leyburn, with the neighbouring village of Spennithorne also close by. Both villages offer a range of community and recreational facilities, while Leyburn provides an excellent selection of independent shops, cafés, pubs, restaurants, professional and medical services. Surrounded by beautiful countryside, the area offers superb opportunities for walking and exploring the Yorkshire Dales, with the market towns of Richmond and Bedale also within easy reach. The accommodation offers a good-sized living room, a well-proportioned kitchen, three bedrooms and a family bathroom. A useful garden room provides additional living or dining space and enjoys views over the garden. There is also a large attached garage, incorporating a built-in utility area and separate WC, providing excellent practical space for storage, laundry and household requirements. The property benefits from efficient oil-fired central heating. Externally, the property benefits from attractive wraparound gardens which are a particular feature of the home. The gardens are well established, with a good selection of mature shrubs, raised beds and lawned areas, creating a pleasant and private outdoor space. The elevated position provides lovely views across the surrounding countryside and towards the hills beyond. A private driveway provides off-road parking for two vehicles and leads to the garage. The bungalow is now in need of updating and modernisation, but offers a particularly good opportunity for a purchaser looking to improve and personalise a property to their own taste and requirements. While the accommodation is well proportioned and perfectly usable in its current form, the kitchen, bathroom, windows and general décor would benefit from modernisation, allowing the new owner to introduce a more contemporary style and potentially improve the layout and finish where desired. The underlying space, gardens, views and location provide an excellent foundation for creating a very comfortable and appealing home. 22 Hargill therefore represents an excellent opportunity to acquire a spacious detached bungalow in a highly desirable village location, with well-proportioned accommodation, efficient oil central heating, attractive wraparound gardens, lovely countryside views and considerable potential for modernisation and improvement. A generously proportioned and characterful dales cottage dating from circa 1690 and offering well balanced three double bedroom accommodation with two reception rooms and a welcoming hall. Being in the centre of Dent and equal distant from the Sun Inn and the church, the choice is yours! . Location: Dent has a thriving community and boasts a well renowned primary school, village store, church, Dent railway station, cafes and public houses. The location is just 5 miles from the many amenities available in Sedbergh, junction 37 of the M6 is within easy reach and the market town of Kirkby Lonsdale is 10 miles away. Property Overview: Built in circa 1690, Church Gate Cottage as the name suggests, is located next to the village church of St Andrew's right in the heart of the village. Improved and updated over the years, the cottage has the benefit of the charm and character of its era blending with modern day comforts of double glazing, brand new central heating boiler and recently installed Hyco electric hot water boiler. Stepping inside, a warm welcome awaits those that view with original flagged flooring, exposed timbers and stone work all showcased in the generous entrance hall; great as a second dining or living space for entertaining friends and family with access into the ground floor living spaces, along with a stone staircase that leads up to the first floor. There is also a handy under the stairs cupboard. The sitting room to the left of the hallway is full of charm with a bay window overlooking the cobble street to the front and two side windows enjoying distant fell views. To complete the character of the room is the open fireplace and a wealth of exposed beams and stonework. The dining room overlooks the church yard to the rear as does the breakfast kitchen, and a cloakroom just off the dining room offers that all important downstairs WC. The breakfast kitchen has two windows both with deep sills and is fitted with a range of wall and base units with complementary working surfaces and a single drainer stainless steel sink. There is a slot in oven and fridge freezer, along with a washing machine. Upstairs opening off the landing are three double bedrooms, bathroom and useful storage cupboard, with bedroom one having an original oak door. All the bedrooms enjoy delightful aspects of village life and distant views. The bathroom has a window, part tiled walls and a radiator and heated towel rail to warm the room. A four piece suite comprises a panel bath with tiled splash back, a panelled shower cubicle with Mira shower, pedestal wash hand basin and WC. A shelved cupboard houses the Hyco electric boiler and central heating boiler with Hive controls. Accommodation with approximate dimensions: . Ground Floor . Its prime location allows easy access to Cambridge (17 miles), London Stansted Airport (around 30 minutes drive), and the M11 corridor. The town boasts a mainline rail station at Audley End (12 miles), with direct links to London Liverpool Street. The town features a vibrant High Street with a popular twice-weekly market, out of town shopping, as well as an array of public houses, cafes, restaurants, social clubs, and hotels. Situated along Mill Lane in the popular village of Trimley St Martin, the cottage enjoys a convenient location for access to local amenities, nearby countryside and the coastal town of Felixstowe, with its seafront, shops, restaurants and transport connections. Located in a private cul-de-sac of individual styled properties, this three bedroom terraced home with double carport to the side is very much a lifestyle purchase situated in a beautiful riverside setting. This unique and individual home in beautiful surroundings that would suit a family looking for a unique setting or alternatively suit a buyer looking for a tranquil property to downsize to. Ebbsfleet international station and Bluewater are with a short drive. Farningham Road rail station is within approximately ten minutes’ walk with services to Victoria and there is a bus stop outside the entrance to the development. Available chain-free,14 Cornwell Road is a contemporary townhouse in Trumpington with a distinctive arrangement of space. Set over three levels, the house combines four-bedroom flexibility with a notably generous living area, while the principal bedroom occupies the top floor with direct access onto a large private terrace. The main living and dining room is particularly successful. A double-height section featuring a mezzanine balcony and substantial roof glazing giving the room a sense of volume and bringing natural light deep into the house, while glazed doors open directly onto the attractive rear garden. There is ample space to accommodate distinct sitting and dining areas without either feeling compromised, providing a picturesque outlook onto the rear garden. The kitchen is separate and practical, with a broad run of fitted cabinetry, extensive quartz work surfaces and integrated appliances. The ground floor space is completed by under-stairs storage and a separate cloakroom. The bedroom accommodation is spread through the upper floors, creating useful separation from the main living space. The principal bedroom has the top floor to itself, with a distinct dressing area, en suite shower room and opening directly onto the substantial terrace, providing a private outside space that is a genuine additional feature of the house. On the first floor, there are a further two double bedrooms one with its own en-suite shower room and the other with access to the main bathroom, while the fourth bedroom is currently arranged as a study with a sliding door to the mezzanine balcony that overlooks the ground-floor living room below, demonstrating how readily the layout accommodates regular home working without taking over the living areas. Outside, the attractive enclosed rear garden has been designed to be relatively easy to maintain, with gravelled areas, established planting and space for outdoor dining. Parking is another practical strength, with both a garage and carport providing considerably more flexibility than is often available with modern Cambridge housing. Trumpington works particularly well for those who need straightforward access into Cambridge, the Biomedical Campus, the wider road network or trains into central London. Cornwell Road is within the established Great Kneighton area, with cycling routes and the Guided Busway providing useful alternatives to the car, while nearby green spaces give this part of south Cambridge a welcome sense of openness. Situated roughly a quarter of a mile from the Addenbrooke's Hospital / Cambridge Biomedical Campus, this property sits just a 12 minute walk, via Hobson Avenue, from the new Cambridge South railway station with, at peak travel times, up to nine trains every hour to central London stations. 120 sqm / 1293 sqf. 161 sqm / 0.04 acre. text: Accommodation in Brief . Ground Floor. Principal Bedroom with En Suite Shower Room | Two Further Bedrooms | Family Bathroom Upper Floor. Lounge/Dining Room | Kitchen | Cloakroom/WC Externally. Stone Terrace | Gravelled Parking Area | Allocated Parking | Woodland Outlook. The Property . Sawmill Barn is an attractive Edwardian stone barn conversion, occupying a peaceful rural position at Broad Oak, close to Ravenglass and the western fringes of the Lake District National Park. Offering approximately 1,367 sq ft of accommodation, the property retains much of the architectural character of its agricultural origins, with substantial exposed timber beams, a dramatic vaulted ceiling and traditional stone elevations. The reverse-level arrangement makes particularly effective use of the original building, with an impressive first-floor living space overlooking the surrounding woodland and three bedrooms positioned on the ground floor. Constructed in traditional stone beneath a slate roof, Sawmill Barn has an appealingly understated exterior, with timber-framed windows and doors complementing its rural character. A gravelled approach provides access to the property and allocated parking, while a broad paved terrace offers an attractive outdoor seating area against a backdrop of mature trees and established greenery. The principal entrance opens into the upper floor, where the accommodation immediately reveals the character and proportions of the original barn. The lounge and dining room is a particularly impressive space, extending to approximately 22 feet in length and distinguished by a striking vaulted ceiling with substantial exposed structural timbers. Traditional roof trusses span the room, creating a wonderful architectural feature and lending warmth and character to the otherwise light, neutral interiors. The generous proportions comfortably accommodate separate sitting and dining areas, providing considerable flexibility for both everyday living and entertaining. Windows positioned around the room introduce natural light and frame views towards the surrounding greenery, while glazed doors with a Juliet-style railing offer an attractive outlook across the woodland. A wood-burning stove, positioned on a dark tiled hearth, forms a welcoming focal point and complements the traditional character of the exposed beams. Adjoining the principal living accommodation, the kitchen is arranged in a practical U-shaped layout, fitted with a comprehensive range of oak-fronted cabinetry and complementary stone-effect work surfaces. A broad peninsula provides additional preparation space and informal seating, while integrated appliances include a dishwasher, electric hob with extractor above and a double oven. A large American-style fridge freezer sits within a dedicated recess, while a stainless steel sink is positioned beneath a timber-framed window overlooking the surrounding trees. The arrangement allows the kitchen to remain conveniently connected to the principal living and dining space, while retaining its own distinct working area. Vinyl flooring provides a practical finish, and the natural timber cabinetry complements the exposed beams of the adjoining room. A separate cloakroom/WC completes the upper-floor accommodation. A timber staircase descends from the living room to the ground floor, where three bedrooms and two bathrooms are arranged around a central hallway. The reverse-level design provides a useful separation between the principal living accommodation and the bedrooms, with the lower floor enjoying a quieter, more private atmosphere. The principal bedroom is a comfortably proportioned double room, finished in neutral tones and incorporating a recessed alcove providing additional flexibility for furniture or storage. An adjoining en suite is fully tiled in contrasting dark and light finishes and benefits from underfloor heating. The suite comprises a bath with shower over and glazed screen, pedestal wash basin and WC, while a window provides natural light and ventilation. The second bedroom is particularly generous in length, offering ample space for bedroom furniture, together with a recessed section that could accommodate a dressing area or workspace. The room's proportions lend themselves to a variety of uses, whether as a guest bedroom, children's bedroom or combined bedroom and study. The third bedroom benefits from windows on two sides, bringing natural light into the space, while glazed double doors open directly onto the exterior stone terrace. This direct access to the outdoors is a particularly appealing feature, making the room equally suitable as a bedroom, home office or additional sitting room. Serving the two further bedrooms, the family bathroom is fully tiled in warm stone-effect finishes, with underfloor heating adding an element of everyday comfort. A generous walk-in shower incorporates both overhead and handheld fittings, while a fitted timber vanity unit with an inset wash basin, illuminated mirror and heated towel rail completes the room. Throughout the property, the combination of traditional stone construction, exposed structural timbers and natural wood finishes reinforces its origins as a working agricultural building. The accommodation is comfortably proportioned and adaptable, with the impressive upper-floor living space providing the principal architectural highlight. Externally . Sawmill Barn occupies an attractive rural setting, surrounded by mature trees and established greenery that provide a peaceful backdrop to the property. Its traditional stone elevations and slate roof sit comfortably within the landscape, while the restrained external detailing preserves the character of the original building. A gravelled area extends alongside the barn, providing access to the property and its allocated parking. Traditional stone boundary walls and established planting complement the setting. A paved stone terrace lies immediately outside the ground-floor accommodation, providing an appealing space for outdoor seating and dining. The terrace is bordered by natural stone edging and enjoys a leafy outlook towards the adjoining woodland, with mature trees providing an attractive sense of enclosure. The outdoor arrangement offers an appealing balance between enjoying the surrounding countryside and maintaining a manageable external space. Local Information . Sawmill Barn occupies a peaceful rural position at Broad Oak, a small hamlet near Ravenglass on the western fringes of the Lake District National Park. Surrounded by beautiful countryside, woodland and the dramatic landscapes of the Cumbrian coast, the setting offers an appealing balance of rural tranquillity and accessibility to nearby villages and towns. The historic coastal village of Ravenglass lies a short drive away, offering traditional pubs, places to eat and a railway station on the Cumbrian Coast Line, providing connections towards Carlisle and Barrow-in-Furness. Ravenglass is also home to the celebrated Ravenglass and Eskdale Railway, which travels through the beautiful Eskdale Valley, while nearby Muncaster Castle and its extensive grounds are among the area's best-known attractions. The surrounding villages of Gosforth, Holmrook and Seascale provide a selection of everyday amenities, including shops, local services and primary schooling. More comprehensive facilities can be found in Egremont, Millom and Whitehaven. The location is particularly appealing for those who enjoy the outdoors, with the Eskdale Valley, Wasdale and the western Lake District offering excellent opportunities for walking, cycling and exploring. The nearby coastline provides a contrasting landscape of beaches, estuaries and coastal walks, while the A595 offers road connections north and south through West Cumbria. Approximate Mileages . text: Home:. * Detached family home set within the peaceful surroundings of Ferney Green. * Four bedrooms with flexible living spaces across a thoughtfully extended layout. * Light-filled kitchen and dining space opening naturally towards the gardens. * Elegant sitting room with large windows framing the surrounding greenery. * Multiple reception areas are ideal for a snug, study or reading room. * Garage/gym, carport and lots of parking . * Generous windows throughout create a strong connection to the outdoors. * A warm and versatile home suited to both permanent living and weekend escapes. Services:. * Mains electricity, gas, water and drainage. * Good broadband speed. * Private driveway parking - lots!. * Council Tax Band G. * Freehold. Grounds and Location:. * Set within mature, private gardens with established planting and lawns. * West-facing aspect enjoying afternoon and evening sunshine. * Peaceful residential setting tucked away from the centre of Bowness-on-Windermere. * Walking distance to local shops, cafés, restaurants and the lake shore. * Excellent access to nearby fell walks and woodland trails. * Conveniently placed for Windermere village and rail connections. * Located within the heart of the Lake District National Park. Three Hollies occupies a rare position where privacy and connection exist in perfect balance. Here, mornings begin with birdsong drifting through open windows, evenings soften beneath golden western light, and every season leaves its own distinct mark upon the landscape beyond. Approached along a peaceful residential lane lined with mature trees and established homes, the first impression is one of quiet elegance. Gardens rich with greenery frame the house beautifully, softening the stone and drawing the eye towards glimpses of distant fells and the lake beyond. There is nothing hurried about this setting. Everything feels settled, grounded and wonderfully timeless. Over the years, the house has evolved carefully and naturally, growing into the warm and versatile home it is today. Original character remains woven throughout, while thoughtful additions have introduced a gentler openness to the flow of everyday life. The result is a home that feels both generous and deeply welcoming, with each space unfolding easily into the next. At its heart lies the kitchen and dining space, filled with natural light and connected beautifully to the gardens outside. It is easy to imagine long breakfasts here as sunlight pours across the table, or evenings gathered with friends after days spent on the water or walking the surrounding fells. During warmer months, doors open naturally onto the garden, allowing inside and outside living to blend effortlessly together. Elsewhere, quieter corners provide places to retreat and unwind. The sitting room feels particularly inviting, with broad windows framing the greenery outside and evening light stretching softly across the room as the day fades. There is a warmth here that feels unmistakably Lakeland. Cosy during winter storms, calm and airy through summer, and always connected to the changing colours and moods of the landscape beyond. Additional living spaces offer flexibility for modern family life. A snug for quieter evenings, a study overlooking the gardens, perhaps a creative space or reading room. The beauty of the layout lies in its adaptability, allowing the home to evolve naturally around the lives lived within it. Upstairs, four beautifully proportioned bedrooms continue the same atmosphere of light and tranquillity. Some gaze out towards distant fells, others across mature trees and gardens that shift gently with the seasons. Morning mist rising beyond the rooftops, autumn colour settling into the surrounding woodland, soft winter frost catching the first light. Every window seems to frame a different moment of the Lake District landscape. The bedrooms themselves feel restful and calm, removed from the pace of everyday life below. Two bathrooms serve the accommodation with ease, making the house equally suited to family living, visiting guests or long weekends shared with friends. Outside, the gardens are wonderfully established and deeply private. Mature planting creates shelter and softness throughout, while open lawns and quiet seating areas invite slow afternoons spent outdoors. There are spaces to follow the sun throughout the day, from peaceful morning coffee beneath the trees to long summer evenings watching the light fade slowly behind the western horizon. The west-facing aspect gives the house a particularly beautiful quality as evening approaches. Golden light spills across the gardens and into the living spaces, while the surrounding landscape takes on the soft glow so characteristic of the Lakes at dusk. It is a home that feels closely tied to the rhythm of nature and the passing of the seasons. Ferney Green itself remains one of Bowness-on-Windermere's most quietly desirable settings. Tucked away from the busiest stretches of the village, it carries a far more residential and peaceful atmosphere, where homes are often held for generations and neighbours know one another by name. Yet despite its calm surroundings, the heart of Bowness remains within easy reach. Independent cafés, elegant restaurants and welcoming pubs line the village streets, while the shores of Lake Windermere offer sailing, paddleboarding and lakeside walks throughout the year. Nearby Windermere village provides further amenities and rail connections, linking the area seamlessly with the wider country while allowing daily life here to feel beautifully detached from it all. For those drawn outdoors, the surrounding landscape offers endless opportunity. Walks begin directly from the doorstep, winding through woodland paths, climbing nearby viewpoints or following quiet lanes towards the water's edge. Days can be spent exploring the central fells, returning home to warmth, stillness and the gentle glow of evening light settling across the garden. The home benefits from a versatile garage currently used as a gym, along with a separate carport providing additional covered parking. At the bottom of the garden there is further parking space for two cars, offering excellent off-road capacity. The sale also includes two garden sheds, which will remain and provide useful outdoor storage. What makes Three Hollies so special is not simply its location or its proportions, but the feeling it creates from the moment you arrive. There is a softness to the atmosphere here. A sense of ease. The kind of home where family gathers naturally, where weekends stretch longer than expected, and where ordinary moments feel quietly elevated by the beauty of the surroundings. It is a place equally suited to permanent living or cherished escapes to the Lakes. Somewhere to celebrate Christmas beside the fire, to host summer lunches spilling into the garden, or simply to step away from the pace of modern life and reconnect with quieter things. In a part of the Lake District where privacy, character and setting are increasingly difficult to find together, Three Hollies offers something deeply special. A home shaped as much by its surroundings as by the lives lived within it, standing quietly amongst the trees above Windermere, waiting for its next chapter to begin. ** For more photos and information, download the brochure on desktop. From churches to hospitals, chemists to museums, casinos to pubs; all your daily needs are only ever a walk away. Why not visit the local Wildlife Garden, close to the Natural History Museum? With culture and cuisine at your fingertips, Stanhope Mews West is supremely situated for those who enjoy a side order of sophistication alongside their accommodation. A remarkable piece of Edinburgh’s architectural heritage, offering grand proportions, exceptional privacy and the opportunity to create one of the capital’s finest family homes. There are houses that impress through size, houses that impress through setting, and occasionally there are properties whose architecture and history give them an altogether different presence. Avallon is one of those rare Edinburgh homes. Set discreetly within substantial mature grounds on Clinton Road, between Morningside and The Grange, Avallon is an exceptional Category A listed Baronial villa attributed to the celebrated Scottish architect David Bryce and dating from circa 1860. Historic Environment Scotland records the property as a Baronial-style villa with service wing, carriage house and lodge, characterised by pink sandstone, crowstepped gables and distinctive Jacobean detailing. David Bryce became one of Scotland’s most important Victorian architects and is particularly associated with the development of the Scottish Baronial style. His best-known works include Fettes College, while he was also responsible for the major nineteenth-century remodelling and extension of the Bank of Scotland headquarters on The Mound, one of the defining buildings of Edinburgh’s skyline. Approached through its private entrance, a sweeping driveway leads through the mature grounds towards the house and an extensive area providing parking for several cars. From the moment of arrival there is an immediate appreciation of just how unusual this opportunity is. Despite occupying a position in one of Edinburgh’s most affluent and coveted residential areas, the house enjoys a remarkable feeling of privacy and seclusion. The principal house extends to approximately 6,136 sq ft (570 sq m) and currently provides 12 bedrooms, three reception rooms and four bathrooms. The scale of the accommodation, however, tells only part of the story. What makes Avallon particularly special is the character and architectural presence of the building itself, together with the opportunity to breathe new life into an important Edinburgh home. The property does require renovation, as might reasonably be expected of a historic house of this age and architectural complexity, but therein lies a significant part of the opportunity. Rather than adapting somebody else’s finished home, the next owner has the chance to work with an extraordinary historic building and create an exceptional residence suited to contemporary family life while respecting the original architectural qualities that make Avallon so distinctive. As a Category A listed property, works would of course be subject to the necessary listed building and planning consents. The current owner has also explored the potential availability of historic-building grant support, something an incoming purchaser may wish to investigate further with Historic Environment Scotland and the relevant authorities. The estate provides further possibilities beyond the principal house. A coach house and ancillary accommodation sit within the grounds, while the separate lodge at 2A Clinton Road provides an additional dwelling with potential to be refurbished for family, guests or other ancillary use, subject to the necessary consents. Historic Environment Scotland's designation specifically encompasses Avallon, its lodge, gates, gate piers and boundary walls. A setting worthy of the house Part of Avallon’s attraction is just how difficult its location would be to replicate. Clinton Road sits between Morningside and The Grange, placing the property within one of Edinburgh’s most desirable and established residential districts. Yet once inside the mature grounds, the scale, greenery and privacy create an atmosphere more readily associated with a substantial country house than a property so close to central Edinburgh. Morningside’s independent shops, cafés and restaurants are within easy reach, together with the Dominion Cinema, Waitrose and Marks & Spencer, while neighbouring Bruntsfield offers an excellent collection of restaurants, cafés, boutiques and independent businesses. For health and fitness, the beautifully restored Victorian Warrender Swim Centre is also nearby, providing a swimming pool, gym and sauna facilities. The surrounding area offers excellent access to green space, including Blackford Hill and the Hermitage of Braid, while The Meadows, Arthur’s Seat and Holyrood Park provide further opportunities to enjoy Edinburgh outdoors. It is this combination that makes Avallon particularly compelling: a beautiful Baronial mansion within substantial private grounds in one of Edinburgh’s most coveted residential areas, while remaining within walking distance of the city centre. Scotland’s extraordinary golfing heritage within easy reach For golf enthusiasts, Avallon also provides an exceptional base from which to enjoy some of the world’s most celebrated golfing destinations. Approximately 21 miles from Edinburgh lies Muirfield, home of The Honourable Company of Edinburgh Golfers and part of East Lothian’s extraordinary collection of historic links courses. Further afield are two names synonymous with world golf: St Andrews, the Home of Golf, and Gleneagles, one of Scotland’s great international golf and country resorts. Gleneagles combines championship golf with a renowned luxury resort set across approximately 850 acres. For an international purchaser in particular, the combination is difficult to match: all the culture, restaurants, amenities and connectivity of Scotland’s capital, with some of the finest golf in the world accessible beyond the city. Outstanding educational opportunities Families are equally well catered for, with access to some of Edinburgh’s best-known independent schools, including George Watson’s College, George Heriot’s School and Merchiston Castle School, alongside highly regarded state schooling. Nearby South Morningside Primary School received exceptional recognition in 2026 when it was named Primary School of the Year at the UK-wide Tes Schools Awards. At secondary level, Boroughmuir High School was the highest-performing state secondary school in Edinburgh in a published 2026 comparison based on pupils achieving at least five Highers, placing 8th in Scotland. James Gillespie’s High School placed 3rd in Edinburgh and 17th nationally on the same measure. Prospective purchasers should independently confirm current school catchment eligibility. The University of Edinburgh, Edinburgh Napier University and the Royal Infirmary campus are also readily accessible. A rare opportunity Avallon is not simply a substantial Edinburgh house requiring renovation. It represents the opportunity to become the next custodian of an important piece of the city’s architectural heritage, restore its grandeur and create an extraordinary private family home for the next chapter of its history. It is exceptionally rare to find a Baronial mansion of this scale, architectural pedigree and presence standing within substantial private grounds in one of Edinburgh’s most affluent and sought-after residential areas, yet remaining so closely connected to the heart of the capital. Properties combining architectural significance, extensive private grounds, substantial parking, additional buildings and this calibre of south Edinburgh address are extraordinarily difficult to find. For the right purchaser, Avallon presents the opportunity not merely to renovate a house, but to reimagine one of Edinburgh’s remarkable historic residences and create a home of genuine distinction for generations to come. Separate lodge house, coach house and ancillary accommodation. Substantial mature private grounds. 12 bedrooms and three principal reception rooms. Excellent access to Edinburgh city centre and airport. Outstanding restoration and modernisation opportunity. World-class Scottish golf, including Muirfield, St Andrews and Gleneagles, within reach. An exceptionally rare opportunity to create a landmark family home

text: “What we've been told by people who have rented here is how much space the house gives you while still feeling really connected to Bristol. There’s room for everyone to have their own space, the garden is great in the warmer months and you can easily walk to local cafés and parks.". The Home. Set behind a traditional stone façade on Bristol Hill, this substantial period home is arranged over three floors, there are four bedrooms upstairs, two bathrooms and a flexible ground floor space where several of the reception rooms have most recently been used as bedrooms as part of the property's previous HMO arrangement. For a residential buyer, there is plenty of scope to return these rooms into reception rooms or office space to create a generous family home. At the front the bay-windowed room is the largest of the ground-floor spaces and would make an excellent main sitting room. Behind this is another separate room which could work particularly well as a dining room, snug, playroom or home office. The kitchen runs out from the rear of the house and is fitted with a long run of white units and plenty of worktop space. There is room for informal seating alongside, while windows to the side and rear bring in good natural light and a door leads directly out to the garden. There is also a toilet under the stairs. The first floor has three bedrooms. The larger rooms have retained their original timber floorboards and benefit from good ceiling heights, while the front bedroom is a particularly impressive space with a wide bay window spanning much of the front elevation. The third room works well as a single bedroom, nursery or study. A spacious family bathroom also sits on this floor, fitted with a bath and overhead shower. The top floor provides another generous double bedroom, naturally lit by two velux windows and set apart from the rest of the house. An additional shower room on this level makes it particularly useful as a main bedroom, guest suite or space for an older child. Overall, the layout gives a new owner plenty of options and the property is offered with no onward chain. Outside space. The rear garden is a good length and currently laid mainly to lawn with fencing to either side, a patio immediately behind the house and a useful garden shed towards the far end. There is also rear access. Living in Brislington. This property is within walking distance of several well-regarded shops and cafes including Grain.Grape a new cafe and win bar which has opened and Deli at Sandy Park. Paintworks is also just a short walk and is home to Miro Lounge and Alex Does Coffee. Tapestry and Lost & Grounded are nationally renowned Bristol breweries with tap rooms, both of which are within walking distance. The area is popular with young professionals and families, being both close to the city centre but also accessible to several parks and larger green areas, such as the Nightingale Valley Nature Reserve and St Annes Wood. Arnos Vale Cemetery is just a short walk away and there are fairly extensive footpaths around the River Avon, which wrap around Brislington through some scenic spots, which includes the popular Beese’s Riverside Bar to the west. The area is also home to several good schools, such as Holymead and Broomhill Infants and Juniors. For commuters, Brislington is well placed, with several buses running through the area including the Park & Ride, as well as routes for cycling and walking to Bristol City Centre. No onward chain. The area is well served by public transport, with local bus services providing connections across Bristol and Parson Street and Bedminster railway stations offering further options for commuters. text: NO ONWARD CHAIN. A spacious two bedroom home with a generous sitting and dining room, two double bedrooms and a wrap around garden. The Introduction - The first viewings are on Saturday 28th November 2026, by appointment only. Offered for sale with NO ONWARD CHAIN. A spacious two bedroom end terrace with a generous sitting and dining room, two double bedrooms all with a wraparound garden. Located in the Beckhill Estate this allows easy access to Meanwood, Chapel Allerton and Leeds City Centre. The generous accommodation is arranged over two floors and includes an entrance hallway, a spacious sitting and dining room, and a fitted kitchen to the ground floor. The first floor comprises a landing, two excellent double bedrooms, a bathroom and separate W.C. The Sitting & Dining Room - The sitting and dining room is a particularly impressive space, offering plenty of room to create distinct areas for relaxing and dining. Large windows allow plenty of natural light into the room, while the electric underfloor heating and electric fire will provide a comfortable atmosphere to this space. The Kitchen & Utility Area - The kitchen is fitted with a range of wall and base units with useful worktop space, room for a freestanding cooker and washing machine and access to the rear garden can be achieved with ease through a timber door. The kitchen is heated by an electric wall-mounted heater. From the kitchen you walk into a utility area that has further cupboards and space for a free standing fridge freezer. This space also houses the electrical RDC board. From here you can then access the hallway which also has a second door into the sitting & dining room. The First Floor - To the first floor, there is a landing with a storage cupboard. The landing gives access to two generous bedrooms, both benefiting from wall-mounted electric heaters. The principal bedroom is particularly spacious and provides plenty of room for wardrobes and additional furniture, while the second bedroom also offers excellent proportions and would work equally well as a guest room home office or additional living space. The bathroom includes a shower enclosure and wash hand basin, complemented by an electric heated towel rail, while a separate W.C. adds further convenience. The Gardens - Externally, the property benefits from established gardens to the front, side and rear, offering useful outside space with mature planting. There is a handy outbuilding located at the top of the rear garden by the road side which is perfect for storing bikes and garden tools. No Chain - A major advantage is that the property is being sold with NO ONWARD CHAIN. This means the seller is not relying on the purchase of another property, which can help make the transaction more straightforward and reduce the risk of delays elsewhere in a chain. Subject to the usual legal and mortgage process were applicable, this may also provide greater flexibility when agreeing exchange and completion dates. The Location - Meanwood has become one of North Leeds' most sought-after residential suburbs in recent years, extremely popular with first time buyers, professionals, couples and families. The area offers an excellent balance between a vibrant local lifestyle and access to green open spaces. Meanwood is home to a strong mix of independent cafes, bars, restaurants, pubs and local shops, while Waitrose and the Northside Retail Park provide convenient everyday shopping. The property is also well placed for access to Windy Hill Park, Meanwood Park, the Meanwood Valley Trail and Meanwood Valley Urban Farm, giving residents a fantastic choice of outdoor spaces, walking routes and a great choice of things to do. Neighbouring Chapel Allerton, Headingley and Moortown are all within easy reach and also provide a wide range of restaurants, shops, leisure facilities and amenities. Leeds City Centre - Another major advantage of this location is the convenient access into Leeds City Centre. Leeds offers a fantastic range of shopping, dining, entertainment and employment opportunities, with destinations including Trinity Leeds, Victoria Leeds, Leeds Kirkgate Market, the Corn Exchange, First Direct Arena and Leeds Grand Theatre. Leeds Railway Station also provides excellent regional and national connections, making this a highly convenient location for commuters and those who regularly travel further afield. To also mention Leeds Bradford International airport which is around a 20 minute drive from this property. In Summary - 55 Beckhill Chase is a spacious and versatile two bedroom home in a popular Meanwood location, offering generous living accommodation, two double bedrooms, gardens and excellent access to local amenities and Leeds City Centre. The added benefit of no onward chain makes this an especially appealing opportunity for buyers looking for a potentially more straightforward move. A viewing is highly recommended. text: A charming and deceptively spacious three-bedroom terraced home, ideally positioned in the heart of Horsforth, just a short walk from the vibrant amenities of Town Street. Arranged over three floors, with a useful cellar, this characterful property combines generous accommodation with attractive period features, including tall ceilings, exposed timber flooring, an impressive cast iron fireplace and exposed stonework. The property offers two well-proportioned double bedrooms, a superb top-floor principal bedroom, a welcoming sitting room, a fitted kitchen and a traditional house bathroom. Externally, there is a low-maintenance courtyard-style garden to the front, off-street parking for one vehicle to the rear and additional permit parking available on the street. An appealing home in a highly convenient location, ideal for those seeking character, space and easy access to local amenities. LOCATION . Horsforth, named as one of the top 10 most desirable postcodes in England and is a prime residential location, popular with families and young professionals alike. The property is within easy reach of an array of excellent amenities including well regarded schooling for all ages, lovely canal & river walks, and the extensive shopping facilities found on New Road Side and Town Street including Morrisons supermarket. Horsforth Hall Park is a great addition to the community with a children’s playground, bandstand, cricket pitch, skate park and bowling green. For commuters, Horsforth Train Station provides services to Leeds, York and Harrogate. Kirkstall Forge Train Station is located down the A65 and offers further means of convenient access into the city (8 mins) and surrounding areas. The Ring Road (A6120) and the (A65) are nearby and provide main road links to the commercial centres of Leeds, Bradford, York and Harrogate, a regular bus service runs into the City Centre and, for the more travelled commuter, Leeds-Bradford Airport is a short drive away. All in all, this location is sought after by a wide variety of buyers and enjoys a strong sense of community and a thriving village atmosphere. GROUND FLOOR . The property opens directly into a spacious and welcoming sitting room, where tall ceilings and a large front-facing window create a wonderful sense of space and natural light. An impressive cast iron fireplace, complete with timber and tiled surround and a gas and coal-effect fire, provides an attractive focal point, enhancing the room’s period charm. Stairs rise to the first floor, while the kitchen is positioned to the rear and is fitted with a range of wall and base units, with space for freestanding appliances. A rear door provides access outside, and a further staircase leads down to the cellar. Exposed stonework alongside the cellar steps adds a distinctive character feature to the kitchen. CELLAR . A generously proportioned and versatile cellar provides excellent additional storage, benefiting from power, windows to both the front and rear, good head height and natural light. Offering potential for a variety of uses or possible conversion, subject to the necessary consents, this useful space adds further flexibility to the property. FIRST FLOOR . The first floor continues the home’s character, with exposed timber flooring extending across the landing and into two well-proportioned double bedrooms, positioned to the front and rear respectively. Both rooms are neutrally decorated and offer comfortable accommodation. Completing this level is the traditional three-piece house bathroom, comprising a bath with shower over, pedestal wash basin and WC, complemented by part-white ceramic tiling. A useful fitted storage cupboard off the landing provides additional practicality. SECOND FLOOR . Occupying the entire top floor is an impressive and private principal bedroom. This well-proportioned, dual-aspect room benefits from dormer windows to both the front and rear, creating generous head height and allowing plenty of natural light to fill the space. Complemented by fitted furniture, the bedroom offers a comfortable and private retreat, completing the accommodation beautifully. OUTSIDE . Perfectly positioned on Suffolk Street Queensway, the development places the very best of Birmingham on your doorstep. The Bullring & Grand Central, Brindleyplace, the financial district and the vibrant Chinese Quarter are all within easy walking distance, together with an exceptional selection of award-winning restaurants, stylish cafés, boutique shopping and cultural attractions. Exceptional connectivity further enhances the appeal, with Birmingham New Street, Birmingham Moor Street and Birmingham Snow Hill stations all just moments away, providing direct links across the UK. An exceptional three/four bedroom detached family home situated within a cul-de-sac location with versatile accommodation and generous gardens. DESCRIPTION. Occupying a desirable cul-de-sac position on the edge of the popular Moorhayes development, 10 Honeysuckle Close is a beautifully presented three/four-bedroom detached family home offering generous and versatile living accommodation, driveway parking for three cars and attractive enclosed gardens. Previously configured as a four-bedroom property, the former owners have combined Bedrooms 3 and 4 to create an impressive guest bedroom, although the original layout could be easily reinstated to suit growing families. The property benefits from a substantial sitting room, created from the former double garage, with potential for a first-floor extension above, subject to the necessary planning consents. The accommodation is both spacious and flexible, with a useful porch leading you to the welcoming entrance hall with access to a cloakroom, fitted with WC, wash hand basin and heated towel rail and storage cupboard with radiator perfect for drying clothes. To the front of the property, the dining room enjoys a bay window and feature fireplace, creating an ideal setting for formal dining. The heart of the home is the impressive kitchen/breakfast room, enjoying views over the rear garden and fitted with an extensive range of matching wall and base units, complemented by a central island with electric sockets, wine rack, additional storage and breakfast bar seating. Integrated appliances include a fridge/freezer and dishwasher, while there is space for a range cooker. The adjoining breakfast area offers plenty of room for everyday dining. Leading from the kitchen is a well-equipped utility room with further storage, space and plumbing for laundry appliances, and direct access to the garden through french doors. The standout feature of the property is the superb sitting room. Converted from the original double garage, this reception space offers generous proportions, a feature electric fireplace, and French doors opening onto the rear garden. In addition, the summer room provides a versatile and light-filled space, overlooking the gardens and benefitting from two sets of sliding doors, making it ideal as a family room, garden room, or entertaining area. On the first floor, the spacious principal bedroom enjoys a front aspect, fitted wardrobes, and an en-suite shower room with shower, WC, wash hand basin and heated towel rail. Bedroom Two is a comfortable double room with fitted wardrobes and a rear outlook. Bedroom Three has been enlarged by combining two bedrooms and now offers a substantial double room with fitted wardrobes and views over the rear garden. Full of character, charm and generous living space, this substantial period home offers a wonderful combination of elegant original features, versatile accommodation and a genuinely welcoming neighbourhood. Situated on a street renowned for its friendly neighbours and lively community spirit, the property is just a 30-second walk from the beautiful Devonport Park, making it an exceptional place to call home. From the moment you step inside, the house reveals the proportions and architectural charm that make period properties so desirable. High ceilings, ornate ceiling roses and a wealth of period features create a wonderful sense of character throughout, while the spacious rooms provide plenty of flexibility for modern family life. The ground floor offers an excellent balance of everyday living and entertaining space. To the front of the property, the generously proportioned lounge provides an inviting place to relax, with its period detailing adding a sense of elegance and warmth. Beyond this, the separate dining room is equally impressive, offering ample space for family meals, dinner parties and special occasions. To the rear, the substantial kitchen and breakfast room forms the heart of the home, with plenty of room for cooking, informal dining and gathering together. A convenient ground-floor WC completes the accommodation on this level. The sense of space continues upstairs, where the first floor is home to an exceptionally generous principal bedroom, a large family bathroom and a further spacious room currently arranged as a study. There is an additional wonderfully versatile room could equally serve as an additional bedroom/craft room, depending on the needs of its next owners. The family bathroom is particularly impressive in its proportions, offering a level of space rarely found in more modern homes. The second floor provides three further bedrooms, together with an additional bathroom, creating a flexible arrangement that lends itself beautifully to family living, visiting guests or working from home. With accommodation extending across four floors, including a substantial cellar divided into three useful areas, there is an abundance of space for storage, hobbies and the changing demands of everyday life. Outside, the property continues to impress with a south-facing courtyard garden, a lovely spot to enjoy the sunshine, dine outdoors or unwind with a morning coffee. The courtyard offers a manageable outdoor space without the demands of a larger garden, while the added benefit of off-road parking, accessed via a roller door, is a particularly valuable feature. What makes this home especially appealing, however, is not simply the house itself but the lifestyle that comes with it. The street has a wonderful reputation for its friendly neighbours and strong sense of community, with celebrations and street parties bringing residents together and creating the sort of atmosphere that is increasingly difficult to find. It is a place where neighbours know one another and where a genuine sense of belonging forms part of everyday life. And with Devonport Park just 30 seconds away on foot, one of the area's most treasured green spaces is practically on the doorstep. Whether it's a morning stroll, time spent outdoors with the family or simply enjoying a little peace and greenery, the park feels like a natural extension of home. Offering approximately 2,849 sq. ft. of accommodation, including the cellar, this is a home of impressive proportions, rich period character and remarkable versatility. Combining beautiful architectural details, generous rooms, practical features and a truly special community setting, it presents a rare opportunity to enjoy the charm of a traditional period property alongside the comforts and convenience of modern living. LOCATION. Harpford is a small and particularly attractive village lying in the Otter Valley and surrounded by beautiful countryside within the East Devon Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. The village is conveniently situated less than a mile from Newton Poppleford, where there is a village shop with post office, a pub, and a primary school, and a Waitrose is less than 2 miles. The Regency coastal town of Sidmouth, is about 3miles, and sits on the spectacular Jurassic Coast, which stretches for 95 miles and is England’s first natural UNESCO World Heritage Site. The town is renowned for its fine golden beaches, local boutiques, art galleries, delis, bakeries, cafés, farm shops, restaurants and pubs. There are several festivals, including a Folk Festival, a Jazz and Blues Festival, and the Sidmouth Sea Fest. Well-regarded schooling in the vicinity includes Exeter College, Colyton Grammar, Exeter School and The Maynard School. Communication links are excellent with a mainline train station at Exeter providing a service to London Paddington in just over two hours, and the M5 is about 9 miles. THE PROPERTY. A useful utility room and guest cloakroom sit conveniently alongside. The elegant, double aspect sitting room features a stone-built fireplace with gas fire, and opens through to the conservatory, a lovely, sunny room with doors leading to the terrace and gardens beyond. There are two further reception rooms on the ground floor, and a double bedroom with a well-appointed en suite bath / shower room. Stairs rise to the first floor where the landing is sufficiently generous to be used as an informal snug or TV area. There are three further double bedrooms together with a family bathroom. Luttrell House feels bright, airy and exceptionally comfortable throughout with well-proportioned rooms, excellent natural light and an easy connection between the principal living spaces and the gardens. OUTSIDE. The setting of Luttrell House is beautiful, with a quiet lane to the front and outstanding views across the Otter Valley to the rear. There is a large wrap around terrace with steps leading to the lawn, which is bordered with mature hedging and well-established shrub beds. A well-stocked lily pond provides the central feature. text: Church View is an outstanding contemporary house with excellent eco-credentials, making it a highly sustainable home. The property offers up to five bedrooms and over 2,400 sq ft of clean, modish décor and fittings throughout. Set in the heart of the charming village of Cheriton Fitzpaine, it features elevations of white render, timber cladding and tall windows, flooding the accommodation with natural light. The main everyday living space is the open-plan kitchen, dining and sitting area, which provides plenty of space for relaxation or in which to entertain guests. Sliding glass doors at the rear open to the decking, while a large full-height window brings further natural light to the room, which has space for a comfortable seating area and a family dining table. The kitchen itself has shaker-style units to base and wall level, a central island with a breakfast bar, a butler sink and integrated appliances, including a dual oven, an induction hob and a retracting extractor fan. Adjoining the kitchen, the utility room offers further storage space, as well as access to the side and into the garage. Also on the ground floor is a w/c and a double bedroom, ideal for multi-generational living or for use as a studio or private snug, if required. Meanwhile, the first floor has an airy landing with a vaulted ceiling and a tall window welcoming plenty of light. There are a further four bedrooms, including the principal bedroom with its en suite shower room and walk-in wardrobe, as well as a private balcony overlooking the rear gardens. One further bedroom is en suite, also with extensive built-in storage and skylights overhead. The upper level is completed by a family bathroom with stylish tiled flooring, a freestanding bathtub and a walk-in rainfall shower. At the entrance to the home, five-bar wooden gates open to the gravel driveway, which provides plenty of parking space and access to the integrated double garage for further parking and workshop space. The gardens are situated mostly to the rear, and feature an area of elevated timber decking across the entire back of the house and two sides, creating an inside or outside extension of the living space. This area is shaded by a timber-framed pergola, making for a relaxed, sheltered outside space for al fresco dining. Beyond the deck there is an area of lawn with borders of various shrubs, wildflowers and mature trees. The Mid Devon village of Cheriton Fitzpaine offers a charming rural setting with a church, renowned primary school, community shop, an award winning pub, doctor's surgery and a parish hall which hosts frequent local events. There are also excellent walking and cycling routes directly from the village. The bustling town of Crediton is approximately six miles away, offering access to a comprehensive range of everyday facilities, including churches, primary schools, banks, a post office, supermarkets, a leisure complex, library, GP surgery, train station, Queen Elizabeth’s secondary school and a traditional high street with independent shops, cafés and eateries. The town hosts a twice-monthly farmers market selling fresh and local produce. Exeter, approximately ten miles away, is the most thriving city in the southwest. It offers a wide choice of cultural activities with the theatre, museum, arts centre and a wealth of decent high street and independent shopping and restaurants, plus a wide choice of supermarkets. Many primary and secondary schools can be found in Exeter, including Exeter School and The Maynard. The area is well connected by road, with the A377 providing access towards Exeter, while rail services to Exeter St. Davids are available from Crediton, where connections can be made to London Paddington and London Waterloo. Cadgwith has its origins in medieval times as a collection of fish cellars in a sheltered south east facing coastal valley with a shingle cove. Fishing subsidised local farmers' livelihoods. From the 16th Century the village became inhabited with fishing as the main occupation. Subsequently houses, lofts, capstan houses and cellars, constructed of local stone or cob walls and thatched or slated roofs, were built along the beach and up the sides of the valley leading to Cadgwith's characteristic Cornish fishing village appearance. In recent times a very small Anglican Church was built dedicated to St Mary. Today Cadgwith functions as a small fishing cove with fishermen seen bringing in their haul and working on their boats. Also the Cove has an extremely popular public house which is home to the famous Cadgwith Singers, who are well known for their repertoire of traditional folk songs. For day to day needs the close by village of Ruan Minor boasts an active community with many clubs, societies and organisations, primary school, local store/post office, Anglican Church, Methodist Chapel and doctor's surgery. Cadgwith Cove is often used as a filming location such as fisherman's apprentice, Harry Potter and just recently Hercules Pirot. In the area is the National Trust's picturesque Kynance Cove, the village of The Lizard, which is mainland Britain's most Southerly Point and the stretches of golden sands at Kennack. Comprehensive schooling is available in the nearby village of Mullion, which lies approximately four miles distant, where there is a doctors' surgery, pharmacy and a good selection of shops. The market town of Helston is approximately ten miles away and includes a good range of amenities having a sports centre with indoor swimming pool and a variety of national shops and supermarkets.
